course_description:
This advanced level course provides a platform to gather, write and produce social justice news stories. The course will outline professional and ethical guidelines on a variety of news narratives including: First Nations People, refugees, asylum seekers, people affected by disability, multiculturalism and religion. The course will explore theoretical concepts for producing human rights journalism in a digitally-disrupted news market and will highlight the role and impact of the journalist in producing human-focussed stories that accurately reflect complex narratives. The course will investigate the notion of reflexivity in news practice and how this is important for the well-being of journalists as well as producing fair and balanced stories. The course will also focus on story preparation and risk mitigation.

The course provides a framework for reporting complex civic including stories from our communities.

learning_outcomes.description: Differentiate and adapt to audience and context.
Deploy writing techniques such as anecdotes, description, quotation.
Use journalistic investigation/research and editing skills at an advanced level.

Engage in critical reflection and constructive critique of your own work and that of others.

assessment_details.title: Community Video Documentary
assessment_details.task_description: Produce a 3-6-minute video story on a civic issue. The civic journalism documentary must accurately and ethically cover a civic issue with creativity and emotion. Stories must be based in Brisbane. All footage must be original. No AI or stock footage will be accepted. No pieces to camera will be accepted as this is a source driven story. Students must submit full interview transcripts as well as information on where and when the interview took place. Read full task description Hide full task description
assessment_details.assessment_security: Open assessment: In this assessment you can use resources such as your notes, course materials, and other tools, including AI, while completing the task. The focus is not on memorising information, but on understanding, applying judgement, and demonstrating your own thinking.
assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
This assignment will be submitted electronically via Blackboard and using EchoVideo .
Before submitting any assignments for this course, you must ensure you have completed UQ's compulsory online Academic Integrity Tutorial.
Please visit this webpage for further advice on how to submit your Blackboard assignment .
Please visit this webpage for further advice on how to submit your EchoVideo .
Important Blackboard submission information
You must click on the Submit button to submit your work for assessment. Academic staff will not see the files if you have merely saved them as a submission in progress. Files that are submitted CANNOT be retrieved for editing and re-submission. Once submitted, they are delivered to the Course Coordinator. It is your responsibility to check the Submission History and confirm your assignment was successfully submitted. To allow for the many possible technical problems with computers and the internet, students are advised to commence assignment uploads at least 3 hours before they are due. If you don’t receive a submission ID, you should regard your submission as unsuccessful. It is your responsibility to check the assignment preview and confirm that the assignment has been successfully submitted. Students should take a screenshot showing the successful submission to confirm that they have followed the correct process.
Important EchoVideo submission information
When you successfully submit your assessment to EchoVideo, you will see text confirming your submission is complete. You will also receive an email confirmation message.
Students are responsible for retaining evidence of submission by the due date for all assessment items, in the required form (e.g. screenshot, email, photo, and an unaltered copy of submitted work).
If either submission was not successful:
Note the error message (preferably take a screenshot). Go to your assignment page and see if it is possible to submit again. If you cannot submit again email your course coordinator immediately with the assignment attached.
Deferral or extension
You may be able to apply for an extension .
The maximum extension allowed is 28 days. Extensions are given in multiples of 24 hours.
Late submission
A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.

assessment_details.title: Open Justice and Court Reporting
assessment_details.task_description: Write an open justice news story from a trip to the courts. The story must be: 600 words. The story must conform to the fundamentals of civic journalism. You must have at least three primary sources in your story. In addition, you can use secondary sources. Primary sources must be interviewed face-to-face. Provide one image (photograph/illustration/artwork) to accompany the story. These must be your original work. You must include an appendix with a reference list of sources and contact details for the interviewee(s) and the date and manner in which the interviews took place. You must also include full transcripts of your interviews. Refer to the marking criteria in Blackboard. Stories must be based on visits to the courts no more than ten days before the due date. Week 7: Understanding the Courts, Justice, and Democracy In this lecture, we look at the practice of reporting from the courts and why this matters to society. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05
Week 7: Court Reporting Assignment Information In this tutorial we will take you through the best way to tackle the court reporting assignment. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05
Week 8: Court Reporting and Building/Fixing the Narrative In this lecture we look at narrative style, structure and techniques in court reporting Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05
Week 8: Workshopping Your Court Report In this session, we workshop your court report to make sure you are on track. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03

Week 9: An Introduction to Video Civic Journalism In this lecture we look at how to break the rules of orthodox journalism in the service of telling stories that matter. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Week 9: Doing Video Civic Journalism Your ideas and storyboarding meeting Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
Mid-Semester Break
Week 10: Baring Your Sole: The Art Affect and Honesty in Civic Journalism Domentaries This lecture will be delivered by Sam Regi. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Week 10: Developing Your Video In this session, you are asked to present your storyboard for feedback from your tutor. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

Week 11: Doing Video Jouranlism: Part Two - Care, Safety, and Respect In this lecture, we focus in working with your chosen talent and the art and practice of the interview. Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04
Week 11: Workshopping Your Video This week, we will be looking at tips and tricks on doing the final assignment. Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04

policies_and_procedures: University policies and procedures apply to all aspects of student life. As a UQ student, you must comply with University-wide and program-specific requirements, including the: Student Code of Conduct Policy Student Integrity and Misconduct Policy and Procedure Assessment Procedure Examinations Procedure Reasonable Adjustments for Students Policy and Procedure AI for Assessment Guide Recording of Teaching Policy and Procedure Learn more about UQ policies on my.UQ and the Policy and Procedure Library . Course guidelines Communication Expectations While you are a student at UQ, all communication must be conducted according to the UQ Student Code of Conduct . The UQ Library has a helpful Communicate and collaborate online module . Email is the primary way for you to send messages to, and receive information from, the School and our staff. You must use your UQ email address (not a private address) to communicate with staff. You should add a clear subject line, including course code, and a 2-3 word statement. You can send email at any time, however, please do not expect responses outside normal working hours (Monday to Friday from ~8am to ~5pm). Emails that constitute bullying, harassment or discrimination against staff contravene the Student Code of Conduct. Emails like this will be reported to the University, and the matter will be pursued as misconduct. Learning activities
